messages:
emma.sales: Hey team — kicking off ACME POC billing + access. They need hosted API keys, a short Dedicated pool gating window, and a Private/VPC control-plane for sensitive telemetry. Can we confirm what we need to provision on our side and what ACME must provide?
raj.se: Quick checklist below. TL;DR: create billing project, seed trial credits, set per-project quota/spendcap, issue ephemeral keys for engineers, and file a Dedicated pool entitlement request if they want reserved throughput. Also need VPC peering/whitelist info for private.
raj.se: Steps (short):
1) sales -> create billing project in org (label: acme-poc-<env>)
2) finance -> seed trial credits (default $3k unless approved)
3) infra -> Dedicated pool gating request (2-3 business days)
4) se -> create ephemeral API keys + add service account for CI/CD
5) customer -> provide VPC CIDR, egress IPs, and contact for VPN/peering setup

taylor.infra: For the Private control plane we need ACME VPC ID + list of public egress IPs to allow back to our management plane. If they want an on-prem package, that's a separate runbook. Dedicated pool: ask if they want capacity guarantee or just burstable — guarantee requires a minimum commit.
linh.finance: On credits/spendcap: default trial credit = $3000. If you want a spendcap lower than credits, we set a hard quota on the billing project (recommended for POC). For anything >$5k we need legal sign-off for prepay or PO. If sales wants a temporary higher cap, escalate to me with customer name and justification.
samantha_acme: Quick q — how do our engineers rotate ephemeral keys? We prefer short TTLs and automated rotation from CI. Also need logs for per-request cost attribution.
raj.se: @samantha_acme we support ephemeral keys via the API. Example to create a short-lived key (TTL 2h):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral_keys
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "project": "acme-poc-trial",
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "scopes": ["inference:generate"]
}
```
Response returns `client_secret` + expiry. We recommend storing in your secret manager and rotating per CI job. Logs: Enable per-project request logs in Console -> Observability -> Export to S3/CloudWatch.
raj.se: Also note: ephemeral keys inherit project quotas/spendcaps. If the project hits limit, keys become rate-limited/disabled.
taylor.infra: Timeline note: Dedicated pool gating typically 48-72 hours once entitlement is approved and billing project exists. VPC peering takes longer if customer needs VPN setup — plan 5-7 business days.
linh.finance: If you want spend protection, we can enable "spend_shield" which blocks token exchanges once quota is hit rather than billing overages. Let me know desired hard cap.
emma.sales: Proposed initial setup for ACME: seed $3k credits, hard spendcap $2k, ephemeral keys for 10 engineers, Dedicated pool request (burstable) — approve?
samantha_acme: That works for us. We need CI rotation docs and proof that keys stop when cap hits — can we get that in writing?
raj.se: I'll paste a short snippet for the rotation + cap behavior into the onboarding docs and link in ticket.
raj.se: Onboarding ticket created: ENG-POC-4421 — contains billing project creation, infra gating, and docs.
deploy-bot: [automated] billing-project created: project=acme-poc-trial, id=proj_9f2a, created_by=emma.sales, ts=1718001299
linh.finance: Noted. I’ve set trial credits = $3000 and hard spendcap = $2000 on proj_9f2a. If they exceed the cap, requests will be blocked and an alert will fire to finance+sales.
emma.sales: Great. Raj/Taylor — can you add the rotation snippet and a 1-pager on what gets disabled at the cap to the ticket? Then we can demo to ACME tomorrow. :thumbsup:
raj.se: On it, will update ENG-POC-4421 by EOD.
taylor.infra: I'll attach the VPC peering runbook and required customer info fields.
samantha_acme: Thanks all — sending VPC CIDR + egress IP list now.
emma.sales: Perfect. Closing loop once docs + ticket updated.
